errors.problem: the tap gloss says the form is the one 'after lam', but in أَرْجُو أَنْ تَرُدَّ it is the subjunctive after أَنْ, which is exactly what the mistake card is teaching (the 'why' says 'After an the verb ends in -a'); the learner gets a contradicting explanation when tapping the key word

errors.problem: known engine quirks, reported once each: (1) a bare ة in English prose is transliterated 'A / at' ('busy takes A / at as well'); (2) a name after the clitics وَ / لِ is capitalised as one word ('Lisāmī', 'Walaylā', 'Waṭāriq', 'Wadānyāl'); (3) الشَّاي is rendered 'sh-shāī' instead of 'sh-shāy'. The Arabic is correct in all cases
errors.fix: engine: render bare ة as 'tāʾ marbūṭa'; split clitic + name as 'li-Sāmī', 'wa-Laylā'; final ـاي as '-āy'

errors.problem: two further engine faults: (1) in the day-70 reading وَاتَّصَلَ is transliterated 'wāttaṣala' as if wa- carried a long ā, whereas the same elision elsewhere is rendered 'wa-ktub', 'wa-staʿmala' (expected 'wa-ttaṣala'); (2) in d66q7 the bare letter ئ in the English prompt is transliterated as nothing, leaving 'a hamza on a yāʾ seat ()'
errors.fix: engine: 'wa-ttaṣala'; render a bare ئ as 'ʾ (yāʾ seat)' or keep the Arabic letter

notes.note: Jordanian is spelt أُرْدُنِيَّة (no shadda on nūn) in line 1 and الْأُرْدُنِّيّ (shadda) in line 8; both spellings exist, but the course should pick one.

notes.path: e.g. day65 dialogue.lines[7].ar 'قَرَأْتُ قَصِيدَة لَهُ'; day63 dialogue.lines[4].ar 'وَكَانَتْ مَدِينَة غَنِيَّة جِدًّا'
notes.note: House style: tanwīn is written on indefinite accusatives ending in a consonant (مَنْسَفًا, تَقْرِيرًا) but never on words ending in ة, even mid-sentence as a direct object (قَصِيدَة لَهُ, مَدِينَة غَنِيَّة, كَلِمَة جَدِيدَة). Consistent, and acceptable at the sentence end, but the owner may want the full ending (قَصِيدَةً, مَدِينَةً غَنِيَّةً) inside sentences in a fully vocalised course.

In every comparative phrase the tap gloss for مِنْ is the generic 'from', while the segs correctly say 'than'. A learner tapping أَكْبَرُ مِنْ gets 'bigger · from'. Not wrong, but a tap gloss 'from; than (after a comparative)' would help.
Tap gloss 'مُدِير=director (of)' adds '(of)' although the word is not in an iḍāfa; 'manager, director' would be cleaner.
رَسَائِل رَسْمِيَّة is translated 'formal emails'; the Arabic says 'formal letters/messages'. Context (day 67) makes 'emails' plausible, so left as a note.

مِنْ فَوْقُ (with ḍamma) is the correct classical form for the cut-off adverb, but it will surprise learners who have only seen فَوْقَ; a seg note 'from above (special ending after min)' would prevent them thinking it is a typo.
Key 'ala-w9' among the newWords looks like an internal id leaking into the list; cosmetic only.

summary: Read the whole export for days 61-70 (comparatives, superlatives, Petra, office, university, phone, email, verb patterns, language exchange, job interview): every Arabic line with its harakat, case endings and agreement, every verb form (subjunctive after أَنْ, imperatives, duals, hollow verbs), all English translations and literals, all seg and tap glosses, all 70 quiz answer keys and the mistake cards. The Arabic itself is clean: no wrong case after إِنَّ/لَيْسَ/كَانَ, correct diptote comparatives (قَبْلَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ), correct numerals (عَشَرَةَ أَفْعَال, خَمْسِ سَنَوَات, ثَمَانِمِئَةِ دَرَجَة), correct feminine subjunctive تَقْرَئِيهَا, and all answer keys are right with no second correct option. I found 11 errors: 2 major, both tap glosses in day 68 that teach the wrong word (دَرَّسَ glossed 'lesson' and اِسْتَعْمَلَ glossed as an imperative) in the very lesson about verb patterns; 9 minor: three missing iḍāfa vowels (مَدِينَة جِبَال, كَلِمَة دِيوَان, كَلِمَة مَدْرَسَة), five tap glosses that carry another sentence's sense (تَرُدَّ 'after lam', قَرِيبًا 'near', الْكِتَابَة 'spelling', مُسَافِر 'passenger', ل 'for', أَكْبَرُ 'bigger' in a superlative quiz), and two engine entries (the known ة / clitic-name / shāī quirks, plus 'wāttaṣala' and an empty '()' for a bare ئ). Pattern: the shared tap dictionary is the weak point; it resolves each Arabic word to one global gloss, so a word taught with a new sense (Form II verb, participle, superlative, 'soon') shows the older or a wrong meaning when tapped, while the per-sentence segs are almost always right. 7 notes for the owner on spelling consistency, tanwīn style and small gloss polish.
